Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The players are out in the middle. Roger Mukasa and Simon Ssesazi to open for Uganda. Alei Nao to bowl first.
...THE CHASE...

For Uganda, they will be on cloud-9 right now. Brian Masaba couldn't have asked for a better performance from his group. All the bowlers whenever asked, stepped up for the team and went with a wicket atleast in the spell. Uganda will be confident to chase this down. Right then! The pitch is not an easy one to bat on. Papua New Guinea will be aware that Uganda got bowled out under 60 in their last match against Afghanistan. Can the PNG bowlers upsring a surprise or it will be a walk in the park for Uganda? Let's find out.

Frank Nsubuga who bowled an exceptional spell is up for a quick chat. He says it was a very big moment for him and it was very exciting. Adds that he has waited 43 years to play his first World Cup game and it's special. Tells that the pitch was holding, and he tried to give flight and bowl wicket to wicket as his coach said. Mentions that it is all about looking after the young guys and they look after him as well. Ends by saying that have a good mix in their squad.

A sorry looking batting card for Papua New Guinea. Really it just didn't look like they were comfortable on this slow pitch. The way their batters lost wickets didn't help them. Papua New Guinea lost three wickets in three overs. Lega Siaka and Hiri Hiri showedtried to retrack the innings but once they both fell, Papua New Guinea fell like a pack of cards. Papua New Guinea have gone a step back with the bat as compared to their performance against West Indies.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Sese Bau is off the mark! A length ball, outside off. Bau drives it aerially and over point. The fielder from third man runs across but fails to stop despite a dive.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Cosmas Kyewuta to Sese Bau, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Leg bye! On a length and on the pads. Ura looks to clip but misses and gets hit on the pads. An appeal follows again for LBW but that was going well down leg. A leg bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Cosmas Kyewuta to Tony Ura, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: A huge appeal for LBW and up goes the finger. Tony Ura walks across, has a chat with Bau and takes it upstairs. No bat involved. Maybe just clipping the leg pole. No, Ball Tracking shows it rolls just above the leg pole. A cross-seam delivery, length and on middle and leg. Ura looks to flick but gets hit on the inside half of the pads. Good review in the end by Ura.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Cosmas Kyewuta to Tony Ura, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Cosmas Kyewuta to share the attack.
A wicket-maiden to start for Alpesh Ramjani and Uganda! Fuller delivery on middle, Sese Bau blocks it out.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Alpesh Ramjani to Sese Bau, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: This is a good start by Alpesh Ramjani! Goes full now, slides it across the batter. Bau drives it but to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Alpesh Ramjani to Sese Bau, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls a bit flat, outside off. Sese Bau goes back to cut but misses it. Two dots in a row.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Alpesh Ramjani to Sese Bau, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowls it full and outside off. Sese Bau leans and pushes it to covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Alpesh Ramjani to Sese Bau, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sese Bau walks out to bat at number 3.

OUT! LBW! An early blow for Papua New Guinea as the skipper goes! Assad Vala has reviewed it. If no bat, that is clearly out. UtraEdge shows no bat. Ball Tracking shows THREE REDS. Out it is! Tossed up, full angling on middle and leg and hint of spin as well. Vala goes back in his crease to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. Assad Vala goes without troubling the scorers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Alpesh Ramjani to Assad Vala, OUT! lbw b Alpesh Ramjani.

Commentary.Commentary: Slides it full and outside off, across Vala who tries to push it across but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Alpesh Ramjani to Assad Vala, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities! We can see the Uganda players in a huddle who spread out to take their respective field positions. Tony Ura and Assad Vala are the two openers for Papua New Guinea. We will see spin straightaway as Alpesh Ramjani has the new ball in his hand. Let's play...

The umpires make their way out to the middle followed by the players of both teams who line up for their respective national anthems. It will be Uganda's first followed by the national anthem of Papua New Guinea.

PITCH REPORT - Katey Martin says that there is humidity and dew will be a factor later while it will also skid on. Adds that the straighter hit is the longest one while the square boundaries even and running between the wickets will be important. Darren Ganga joins her and says that it is not that dissimilar to the last game as there will be turn but the pacers will get swing upfront as well. Tells that batting in the middle phase will be crucial and whoever wins, history will be created.
Papua New Guinea (Playing XI) - Tony Ura, Assad Vala (C), Lega Siaka, Sese Bau, Hiri Hiri, Kiplin Doriga, Charles Amini, Norman Vanua (In place of Kabua Morea), Alei Nao, Chad Soper, John Kariko.

Uganda (Playing XI) - Simon Ssesazi, Roger Mukasa, Robinson Obuya, Dinesh Nakrani, Riazat Ali Shah, Alpesh Ramjani, Kenneth Waiswa (In place of Ronak Patel), Brian Masaba (C), Juma Miyagi (In place of Bilal Hassan), Cosmas Kyewuta, Frank Nsubuga (In place of Henry Ssenyondo).

Assad Vala says he was 50-50 on what to do but is happy to bat first. Adds they spoke after the game against the Windies, they know where they need to improve. Feels they play some good cricket against a Test playing nation. Informs they have made one change.

Brian Masaba says that they will bowl first. Adds that their batting performance in the last game was nothing to do with the pitch and they will like to chase. Mentions that they had a chat as a batting group and everyone is on the same page and they will look to put on a better performance. Informs they have made a few changes.
TOSS - Uganda have won the toss and will BOWL first.

It was not the same though for Uganda who took some real beating from the hands of Afghanistan. Both, Papua New Guinea and Uganda have announced themselves on the big stage but who gets off the mark is going to be crucial here. How will the associate teams go against each other? Will Papua New Guinea put the extra effort this time or Uganda will bounce back in style? We will find out soon. Toss and team news coming up.

Hello and welcome to the match number 9 in the ICC T20I World Cup where Papua New Guinea will take on Uganda in Group C. Both teams have played a match each already. Papua New Guinea on the opening day as they faced the Windies but came out on the losing side. They though announced themselves by playing some quality cricket and made the Windies work hard for the two points.
...Match Day....

The ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024 continues to deliver excitement, and now it's time for match number 9, featuring an all-associate clash between Papua New Guinea and Uganda at the Guyana National Stadium. Both teams, placed in Group C alongside heavyweights West Indies, Afghanistan, and New Zealand, are hungry for their first win after opening game defeats. Papua New Guinea faced the West Indies in their first match, putting up a valiant fight despite falling short. Their bowlers made the tournament hosts work hard for each run, showcasing resilience. Alei Nao stood out in the pace attack, while Assad Vala and John Kariko excelled in the spin department. For PNG to succeed, contributions from Kabua Morea, Chad Soper, and Charles Amini with the ball will be crucial. On the batting front, Sese Bau was a standout performer, with Assad Vala and Kiplin Doriga providing valuable support. However, Tony Ura, Lega Siaka, and Hiri Hiri will be eager to make a stronger impact. Uganda, on the other hand, had a challenging World Cup debut against Afghanistan. They just could not turn up with the bat, as the Afghan attack proved too strong for them. Roger Mukasa, Simon Ssesazi, and Riazat Ali Shah have been the mainstays of Uganda's batting over the past year and will carry the scoring burden. Alpesh Ramjani, a key player in Uganda's qualification journey, will need to contribute with both bat and ball. Cosmas Kyewuta and skipper Brian Masaba were the stars with the ball against Afghanistan and will look to carry that momentum forward. However, if Uganda are to get the better of Papua New Guinea, the likes of Alpesh Ramjani, Bilal Hassan and Henry Ssenyondo will have to bowl as a unit. Whichever team wins, one thing is certain, we will witness history in the making, as the victor of this clash will secure their first-ever win in a Men's World Cup. Who are you rooting for?
